summary.text: 贵 is the simplified form of 貴. The traditional graph is glossed as “not cheap”; current meanings include “expensive” and “valuable.” Its early construction is disputed.

formation.text: The traditional dictionary analysis treats 貴 as a phonosemantic compound: 貝 contributes a money-related meaning, while 臾 supplies the sound. Another account describes early forms as hands holding earth and assigns the sound role to 中. The early depiction and sound element remain disputed.

components.text: In the traditional analysis of 貴, 貝 contributes a money association. The dictionary describes it as a shell used as currency; this does not establish that the early graph depicted hands carrying a shell.

The traditional dictionary identifies 臾 as the sound element and calls it an ancient form of 蕢; a later study associates it with the protoform of 簣. The historical sound link to 貴 is not demonstrated by a comparative reading series.

sound_limitation.text: The cited analyses assign 臾 a phonetic role but do not provide a supported reading pair establishing its historical sound relation to 貴.

components.text: A competing account describes early forms as hands holding earth and assigns 中 the sound role, unlike the traditional analysis with 臾.

sound_limitation.text: This account provides no historical reading comparison for 中 and 貴. Their modern Mandarin readings, zhōng and guì, do not establish an ancient sound relation.

sound.text: The modern Mandarin readings are zhōng for 中 and guì for 貴; this comparison records current pronunciation only.

history.text: References present oracle-bone, bronze, seal, and standard forms, but their descriptions do not settle the early graph’s details. The later variant 䝿 is described as a regularization of a small-seal form; other transmitted spellings may reflect graphic distortion.
贵 is the simplified counterpart of 貴; the adoption date of this particular form remains unresolved.

uncertainties.text: The early graphic analysis is disputed: one account describes hands holding earth and assigns 中 the sound role, while the traditional dictionary and a scholarly analysis identify 貝 and 臾. These accounts do not resolve the original depiction or sound element.
The chronology connecting price, social rank, worth, esteem, and honor is unresolved; independently dated primary-text examples have not established it.

senses.text: A traditional dictionary glosses 貴 as “not cheap”; current records also give “expensive” and “costly.” The dating of this sense in primary texts is unresolved.
Current dictionary records include “valuable” and “precious.” Their dating and whether they developed directly from “expensive” are unresolved.
Dictionary records include esteem, honor, and high social status. Their chronology and semantic path from the price sense are unresolved.

limitations.text: The traditional gloss “not cheap” and current senses are supported, but a dated sequence among them is not. Reported classical examples have not been verified against primary texts.

overview.text: 贵 is the simplified form of 貴, glossed as “not cheap” in a traditional dictionary and now used for “expensive” or “valuable.” Accounts differ over the early graph’s depiction and which part supplied its sound.

components.text: In 貴, 貝 links the traditional analysis to shells used as money and their association with value.
The traditional analysis names 臾 as the sound element, but its historical sound link to 貴 is not demonstrated.
An alternative account describes hands holding earth and assigns 中 the sound role; this analysis is disputed.

relationships.text: In the traditional dictionary analysis of 貴, 貝 contributes an association with money and value.
The traditional dictionary and scholarly analysis identify 臾 as the sound element in 貴; an alternative analysis of the early graph remains disputed.
An alternative paleographic account assigns 中 the sound role in 貴, differing from the 臾 analysis.
贵 is the simplified form of 貴.
